newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Romania will send special envoys to NATO member- countries which have so far failed to express their support for Romania's integration into the alliance.

* A series of former dignitaries of the defunct Romanian Communist Party are still living in luxury state-owned houses, Valerian Stan, the head of the government's control body, told a news conference.
He said the government will demand an inquiry in the case of ex-president Ion Iliescu and 33 other dignitaries who illegally purchased state protocol houses.
* Senate chairman Petre Roman met representatives of Israel's 400,000-strong community of Jews born in Romania.

Roman said Romania was determined to allow the restitution of Jewish community properties confiscated by the communists. He said Romania will also look into possibilities to give Romanian Jews compensations for their confiscated property.

* Former president of state-owned bank Bancorex SA, Razvan Temesan, told a Senate commission that more than 100 people related to the former ruling Party of Social Democracy took loans from the bank, Democratic Party senator and member of the commission Nicolae Dide said.

* The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe's High Commissioner Max Van der Stoel arrived for a two-day visit to Romania to assess the country's human rights and minority rights situation. Van der Stoel had talks with Marko Bela, the leader of the Hungarian Democratic Union.
